page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.m2.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. The hardware profile is built on the x86_64 architecture and provides 8 dedicated vCPUs coupled with 64.0 GB of system RAM. This delivers a memory allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, tailoring the server to computational processes that require substantial working memory space relative to processing threads.

The hardware configuration includes no local storage volumes, requiring system and application disks to be provisioned via external network-attached storage. It contains no GPU accelerators and does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Consequently, operations requiring specialized hardware acceleration or low-latency local NVMe scratch space are not supported by the base configuration.

Resource allocation on this profile emphasizes memory density over compute concurrency, avoiding the financial footprint of provisioning unnecessary CPU cores when memory capacity is the primary operational constraint. The server is suited for memory-intensive workloads, including in-memory key-value databases, memory caching servers, distributed processing nodes, and intermediate data transformation pipelines.

The configuration provides 8 dedicated vCPUs paired with 64.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not feature local storage volumes or hardware GPU accelerators, necessitating remote block storage solutions for disk operations. From a resource standpoint, this allocation model prioritizes high RAM capacity relative to processor density, avoiding unnecessary CPU allocation costs for footprint-heavy services. The configuration contains no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Given its high memory-to-CPU ratio and absence of bundled local disks, the ecs.m2.xlarge is designed for memory-intensive enterprise tasks, such as in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, data processing runtimes, and intermediate ETL aggregation pipelines.
